_note: The habitat's own hardware, read through Home Assistant. Each entry is one entity to poll and show inside the station's Habitat panel (under the node's tiles, headed Habitat hardware): id is the entity id without the 'sensor.' prefix, label is what the station shows, unit is a fallback when Home Assistant does not name one, kind is 'gauge' (reads as it is) or 'counter' (only ever rises, like an energy meter — the tile then also says what today has added), decimals is how the value is printed, an optional chart names the chart the device is drawn on (devices with the same chart and unit share it — NO₂ and CO on "Air quality"), an optional span (the least height of the chart's Y axis round the readings, in the unit — oxygen keeps 2 percentage points so a steady reading has room to move), and an optional range [lo, hi] fixes the Y axis of the chart the device is drawn on (temperature charts are 0–30 and energy charts 0–300 unless a device says otherwise). Add a sensor here and it is on the station within a minute — no restart, no redeploy. WHERE Home Assistant is and the API token live in .env (HA_HOST, HA_PORT, HA_API_TOKEN), never in this repository. THE HABITAT SENSOR: the `habitat` block maps each channel of the Habitat panel — co2, temp, hum, pres, voc, iaq and iaqc (the air quality index's readable classification) — to the Home Assistant entity that feeds it (without the 'sensor.' prefix). While Home Assistant is configured and this block is filled, the Habitat panel, the ticker, the booklet and the record read the habitat from these entities (every HABITAT_POLL_MS, a minute by default) instead of the external node; empty it, or set HABITAT_SOURCE=node, to go back to the node.
